newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ALPINE SKIING-SYKORA KEEPS THE SPOTLIGHT WITH FIFTH WIN.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-SYKORA KEEPS THE SPOTLIGHT WITH FIFTH WIN.

text.p: Austria's Thomas Sykora continued to hog the spotlight with his fifth World Cup slalom win of the season on Sunday.

The lanky Austria has dominated the slalom this season the way Italian Alberto Tomba once did, winning five of the six races so far. The only blemish on his otherwise perfect record was a second place in Breckenridge.

On Sunday, while world and former Olympic champion Tomba stayed at home to recover from influenza, Sykora extended his lead in the slalom World Cup standings to 220 points with just three races to go and 300 points still on offer.
Sykora, who led by 0.26 seconds over team mate Thomas Stangassinger after the first run, produced only the sixth best time on his second trip down the deteriorating Lauberhorn course.
But it was still more than enough as the 28-year-old Austrian collected his seventh career win with a two-run combined time of one minute 34.03 seconds.

"This is the most difficult slope and I really wanted to win here," said Sykora, who can wrap up the World Cup slalom title with a second place finish in Kitzbuehel next weekend. "In the second run I knew Stangassinger was ahead and I decided to risk it all for victory.
"I made some mistakes but once you've won they all become perfect runs. Now I can look forward to Kitzbuehel where I had my first win last year."
For Stangassinger it was the third time this season that he had to settle for second behind his team mate, finishing in 1:34.36.

"It looks like I'm always the crown prince behind Thomas," said Stangassinger. "I seem to always finish second but I know that I am very close to Thomas, I know I have a chance. Maybe I'll win in Kitzbuehel or if not maybe (at the world championships) in Sestriere."
Third place went to reigning World Cup slalom champion Sebastien Amiez of France with 1:34.68. Norway's Kjetil Andre Aamodt was fourth with 1:35.01.
"I'm third, again, behind the Thomases," said Amiez, who has occupied the bottom step of the podium three times this season. "But this time I was much closer.
"I'm happy about this result because the slope here is very difficult and once you've achieved a podium here you know anything is possible the next race."
Tomba, twice a winner in Wengen, is expected to compete in Kitzbuehel.
After crashing heavily in pre-season training and injuring a wrist and knee, Tomba has struggled to get back to his old form and has completed only two slaloms this season.
The flamboyant Italian was second behind Sykora in his season's debut at Madonna di Campiglio before Christmas and was eighth in his only other race in Kranjska Gora.
Sykora now has 580 points in the slalom standings with Stangassinger second on 360.
Switzerland's Michael von Gruenigen skied a brilliant second run to move from 21st after the first leg to ninth, allowing him to cling on to the lead in the overall standings.
The giant slalom specialist tops the overall rankings with 606 points, just five ahead of Aamodt.
